subject: Meteorology
title: How Hail Forms
description: A 60-second lesson on How Hail Forms.

hook.text: Hailstones grow inside thunderstorm updrafts—cycled up and down, adding layers of ice with each trip.

buildup.text: A frozen raindrop is carried upward by the updraft, collecting supercooled water that freezes on contact.

discovery.text: Clear and opaque layers form because wet growth (clear) and dry growth (opaque) alternate as the stone travels.

twist.text: The stone doesn't bounce up and down many times—it mostly grows in one long ascent through varying conditions.

climax.text: Hail falls when it grows too heavy for the updraft—stronger updrafts produce larger, more dangerous hailstones.

punchline.text: The stronger the updraft, the bigger the ice it can hold.

quiz.question: What determines how large hailstones can grow?
